noticias.titulo: Google resolves cloud outage affecting UK banks and websites
noticias.resumen_propio: A failure at Google Cloud's London-region facility, traced to a power problem in one of its smaller data center zones, disrupted online banking apps and several UK websites on a Tuesday morning. Users flooded outage monitors with complaints, and the company said services were restored by evening. The article also links this event to a similar outage a year earlier and notes how small businesses suffered losses.

noticias.titulo: UK government to make Jackdaw gas field announcement
noticias.resumen_propio: The British government is expected to decide whether to approve two North Sea fossil fuel projects after months of delay. Reports suggest the Jackdaw gas field will get the green light, while the Rosebank oil field may wait. Environmental groups oppose more drilling because of its climate effects, whereas industry bodies say production would bring jobs and strengthen energy supply amid overseas conflicts. Earlier licences were challenged in court over emissions from burning the extracted fuel.

noticias.titulo: Paddy Power cuts 1,400 jobs and blames betting tax rises
noticias.resumen_propio: Flutter, the owner of Paddy Power, plans to cut up to 1,400 roles and blames higher gambling taxes that it says it cannot fully bear. The firm reports a worldwide quarterly loss while its UK and Irish revenues grew, and it projects large profit hits from the tax changes. Further duty increases on online sports betting are scheduled for next year.

noticias.titulo: Government failings allowed Covid 'to spread like wildfire' in care homes, inquiry finds
noticias.resumen_propio: An official UK inquiry's sixth report concludes that government failures in care settings let Covid spread quickly among residents and staff in the early pandemic. It cites shortages of protective equipment, risky hospital discharges into homes, harmful visiting limits, and a large death toll, and it reminds readers how many adults depended on care services when the outbreak began.

noticias.titulo: Union attacks NatWest plans to get workers back to the office
noticias.resumen_propio: A labor union objects to a bank's decision to require more in-office days from its staff, arguing the change will raise commuting and childcare costs for lower-paid workers and disrupt disabled employees and carers. The bank defends the shift as helping teams collaborate and says it will give colleagues time to adjust.
